rules.statement: A Roman Catholic Archbishop, appointed by the Pope of Rome, is not necessarily a corporation sole with perpetual succession under local or English law.
rules.supporting_quote: "It is argued that a Bishop of the Anglican Church in England is a corporation sole with perpetual succession, where, though the individual changes and a successor is appointed from time to time, as need may be, by the Sovereign, so far as concerns the property of the corporation the Bishop never ceases to be, and continues for ever without any breach. The two cases are not analogous. I cannot find that the English Courts, or our Courts, have ever recognized the creation of a body corporate by the authority of the Pope of Rome, and no such authority has been cited to us in the course of the argument of this case."
